subject: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth private VPC & air-gap requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth private VPC & air-gap requirements

John — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared:
- Strict data residency: PHI must remain in your US-controlled VPC or on-prem environment (no third-party cloud multi-tenant storage).
- Air-gapped lab requirement for certain models (research/QA workflows) with no outbound internet egress.
- Network constraints: strict firewall rules, limited outbound ports, and an internal proxy for package updates.
- Audit & key management: you need KMS/HSM integration and detailed audit logs for token usage and access.

Goals we heard:
1) Proof-of-concept: run a Redwood Private deployment inside AcmeHealth VPC with a small model serving pipeline for triage/summary workloads.
2) Security review: ensure SOC2 controls map, provide evidence for logging, and show KMS/HSM integration options.
3) Deployment path: evaluate an air-gapped option for model QA and an online VPC-hosted path for production.

Open questions / assumptions:
- Network: can your infra team open outbound to our package mirror IP range for controlled updates, or do we need to support an offline package bundle? (Neha: placeholder for technical options)
- Data flows: will the customer-managed KMS be accessible from the instance, or do you require HSM appliances on-prem?
- Timeline: you mentioned an internal compliance review in early March — is that still the target?

Attachments: I attached our Private solution brief, an architecture diagram, and a short security checklist.

Proposed next steps:
- Technical workshop (1.5 hours) with AcmeHealth infra + security + Neha (solutions eng) — goal: validate network plan and package/update approach.
- Deliver a tailored deployment plan + cost estimate week of Feb 22.
- Prepare security evidence (SOC2 summary, logging samples) for your review.

Can we lock in a tech workshop next Tue/Wed (Feb 17/18) afternoon PT? If those times don't work, send a couple of alternatives and we'll accommodate.

Thanks — looking forward to continuing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

From: John Doe <john.doe@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Lisa Park <lisa.park@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Security <sec-team@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth private VPC & air-gap requirements

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. This looks right to me. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For the air-gapped lab: we cannot allow any outbound connections from those nodes. Package updates must be delivered via an internal artifact repository or via physical media for the POC.
- KMS: we plan to use an HSM-backed KMS that is only reachable from our private network; an agent-based key proxy is a possibility. We'll confirm details with infrastructure.
- Compliance timeline: our internal review is Feb 26, so having the deployment plan and security evidence by Feb 22 would be ideal.

We can do the technical workshop on Wed Feb 18 at 10:00am PT. Attendees from our side: Lisa Park (infra), Aman Singh (network), and 2 folks from security (sec-team@acmehealth.com).

Thanks — sending over a calendar invite now.

—John
Director, Engineering 
Acme Health

John — confirmed, thanks. Workshop scheduled: Wed Feb 18, 10:00am PT (calendar invite sent). Neha will lead the technical portion and bring our offline-install options (artifact bundle + install guide) as well as a secure package mirror approach that works with restrictive egress.

Action items I/O: 
- Redwood (Neha): prepare offline package bundle + docs, draft deployment plan, and short checklist for HSM integration (deliver by Feb 22).
- Redwood (Marissa): security artifacts pack (SOC2 summary, logging examples, response playbook) and cost/estimates (deliver by Feb 22).
- AcmeHealth: confirm whether the HSM KMS will allow an internal proxy agent or requires appliance-only access; share any firewall rules that would block our mirror IPs if you have them.

I'll follow up after the workshop with the combined plan and next-step timeline. Appreciate the quick turnaround from your team.

Best,
